model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the coverage achieved by three variants of the Llama model—Llama-3B, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—as a function of the number of completions, denoted as k. The x-axis represents the “Number of completions (k)” on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 2^0 (1) to 2^5 (32), with tick labels at each power of two. The y-axis represents “Coverage,” scaled linearly from 0.4 to 0.8. The blue line with solid circles represents Llama-3B, starting at a coverage of 0.4 when k=1 and increasing to 0.8 when k=32. The green line with triangle markers represents Llama-1B, starting at approximately 0.35 when k=1 and reaching approximately 0.82 when k=32. The light blue line with diamond markers represents Llama-1B + FT, starting at approximately 0.3 when k=1 and reaching approximately 0.8 when k=32. All three lines show an increasing trend in coverage as k increases, with Llama-3B and Llama-1B reaching higher coverage values than Llama-1B + FT at the highest k value.
